domain: Religious Studies / Halakhic Theory / Commitment System Analysis
topic_summary: Analysis of rabbinic preservation of Temple sacrifice law (Kodashim) across 1,900 years without performance. The study-as-substitute doctrine creates a boundary collapse between exercising a commitment and archiving its symbol, raising questions about whether continuous study of unperformable ritual constitutes occupation of a living kernel or maintenance of an empty husk.

key_entities: Kodashim (fifth order of Mishnah/Talmud, 11 tractates on Temple sacrifice)
Second Temple (destroyed 70 CE, ending sacrificial practice)
Babylonian Talmud (Gemara on Kodashim motivated by study-as-substitute doctrine)
Maimonides (12th century, codified Kodashim despite practical irrelevance)
Rabbinic academies (post-70 CE institutions maintaining sacrificial study)
key_tensions: Study vs performance: intellectual engagement with laws vs physical execution of ritual
Eschatological suspension: laws studied as if performable yet performance indefinitely deferred
Historical contingency vs eternal validity: Maimonidean claim that sacrifices are both time-bound accommodation and timeless law
key_mechanisms: Study-as-substitute doctrine: Talmudic principle that studying sacrifice laws equals performing them
Messianic deferral: Temple restoration tied to messianic expectation, creating permanent temporal suspension
key_absences: No Jerusalem Talmud on Kodashim; briefer Babylonian Gemara than other orders—suggests practical irrelevance recognized even within tradition

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The divine commandment to perform Temple sacrifice as prescribed in Torah
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Rabbinic interpretive authority grounded in Oral Law transmission and halakhic reasoning

readings.commitment: Study of sacrifice law IS the exercise of the commandment; intellectual engagement fulfills divine obligation
readings.authority_grounding: Talmudic doctrine that study equals offering; Maimonidean codification as eternal law
readings.expected_structural_delta: Zero extractiveness—study is intrinsically valuable worship; no victim set; beneficiary is the scholar-worshipper

readings.commitment: Sacrifice commandment requires physical execution; without Temple, commandment is suspended not fulfilled
readings.authority_grounding: Literalist reading of Torah prescription; early Reform critique of rabbinic substitution
readings.expected_structural_delta: High extractiveness—1,900 years of study labor directed at unperformable acts; victim is scholarly attention diverted from living law

readings.commitment: Study preserves technical knowledge for future Temple restoration; messianic preparation not present worship
readings.authority_grounding: Eschatological expectation; rabbinic merit-seeking for Temple rebuilding
readings.expected_structural_delta: Moderate extractiveness—study justified by future utility but present value uncertain; beneficiary is future generation

axiom_contradictions.basis: Study-as-performance holds that intellectual engagement fulfills the commandment; performance-only holds that only physical execution fulfills it. No single framework can hold both: either study IS worship or it is NOT worship.

omegas.description: Does the study-as-performance reading genuinely occupy the kernel, or does 1,900 years of study without performance prove the kernel is empty? The boundary between exercising a commitment and archiving its symbol may be indeterminate—study could be both simultaneously.
omegas.source: Kernel/reading decomposition; D1/D4 boundary case recognition

omegas.description: Is messianic expectation (archive_maintenance reading) sincere preparation or post-hoc rationalization? If rabbis genuinely expected Temple restoration, why no Jerusalem Talmud on Kodashim? Temporal suspension may mask kernel abandonment.

Early Reform claim that Maimonides had 'no option but to include' sacrifices suggests performance_only reading. But if study is empty formalism, why 1,900 years of continuous engagement? Extractiveness assessment depends on whether study has intrinsic or only instrumental value.

Is this a commitment system at all, or a post-destruction adaptation that only mimics CS structure? The kernel (sacrifice commandment) may be genuinely contested, or the contest may be between a living kernel (study) and a dead one (performance). Classification instability.
omegas.source: CS recognition boundary case; suspended_kernel pattern uncertainty
